conclusions: Both independent live runs expose the source-constrained Lava, Rocks, Lava, Rocks warning cycle.
All four observed Lava warning paths become persistent terrain-id-3 tiles on the following board; the historical bridge serialized that final-island terrain as water.
Both observed Rocks warning sets become Fire tiles on the following board.
In the second run, the turn-two Rock on (6,5) destroys queued Scarab2 uid 751 before its attack; the recorded player plan leaves that pawn alive before End Turn.
limitations: The historical recording schema does not attest executable, depot, scripts-revision, or map-revision identity, so these runs corroborate but do not build-key the current Windows source inventory.
The old bridge warning order is not treated as proof of native Locations order because it did not export the environment list atomically.

No historical warning placed a Massive, flying, Shielded, Frozen, Building, Mountain, Pod, or corpse edge case on Lava; those rules remain source/general-terrain-derived simulator contracts with focused tests.
The phase-four aftermath is the stage handoff, so neither run observes a fifth selection or an empty LavaStart call.
